exactProducer: conflict-engine.js analyzeConflictPair, invoked by pipeline.js Step 9 fourPartDoctrineTest for every pair among the first ten reranked chunks
exactConsumer: services/conflict-trust-classifier.js classifyConflictState; it correctly maps an incomplete upstream hasConflict=true signal to trust.conflictState=POTENTIAL_CONFLICT and public hasConflict=false
exactCondition: sameIssueGate passes on shared lexical VAT signals and a shared substantive dimension; oppositeHoldingGate passes on taxable/subject versus exempt/not-subject polarity; the engine has no prerequisite that the two inputs represent distinct authority positions

exactInput.sourceKind: Adjacent or overlapping chunks of one statutory record

trustContractViolation: The upstream conflict evidence violates the semantic precondition that a conflict requires two identified authority positions. Complementary fragments within one NIRC §106 record are not two authorities merely because local lexical polarity differs. The classifier and frontend faithfully fail closed on the invalid upstream signal.
generalizationRationale: Chunking can split any statute, regulation, case, or issuance across exceptions, general rules, deemed transactions, effectivity clauses, or remedies. A source- and normalized-reference identity guard applies to all authority types and queries without VAT-specific terms. Structured position, version, effectivity, amendment, or supersession metadata must permit genuinely distinct positions within a consolidated record.
genuineBehaviorToPreserve: Same-issue opposite positions from distinct authority records
Verified conflict classification when complete metadata exists
Justified potential conflict for incomplete but genuine two-position evidence
Same-record positions explicitly distinguished by structured version or effectivity metadata
Authority-support derivation independent of conflict state
Fail-closed source-only, bare-list, missing, malformed, or ineligible answerSupport behavior
candidateHypothesis: Before lexical same-issue/opposite-holding signals may establish conflict, reject a pair whose normalized source identity and normalized legal reference are both the same unless both inputs contain structured metadata that identifies distinct positions, versions, temporal scopes, amendments, or supersession states.
